settings.name_in_paper: Linear Stochastic Bandits (single task, BIAS-OFUL with fixed bias h)
unmapped: the learner (oracle) knows the distance ||h - w*||_2 between the bias vector and the true parameter, used in the confidence radius
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t\in[T]$, the learner is given a decision set $\mathcal{D}_t\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ from which it has to pick an arm $\mathbf{x}_{t}\in\mathcal{D}_t$. Subsequently, it observes the corresponding reward $y_t = \mathbf{x}_{t}^\top \w^* + \eta_t$ ... sub-gaussian random noise term $\eta_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: LTL with Linear Stochastic Bandits (transfer regret over task distribution rho)
unmapped: meta-learning / learning-to-learn: N previous tasks sampled i.i.d. from an unknown task distribution rho, with their datasets available when facing task N+1
the regularisation lambda is tuned as 1/(T Var_h), i.e. the learner knows the task-distribution variance around the bias
settings.definition_quote: We assume that each learning task $\w\in\mathbb{R}^d$ representing a linear bandit, is sampled from a task-distribution $\rho$ of bounded support ... $\mathcal{A}$ trained over $N$ datasets has small transfer-regret: $\mathcal{R}(T,\rho) = \mathbb{E}_{\w\sim\rho}\Big[\mathbb{E}\big[ R(T,\w)\big]\Big]$

algorithms.name: AVG-OFUL (BIAS-OFUL with bias = average of estimated task parameters)
RR-OFUL (BIAS-OFUL with bias = global ridge regression)

bound.expression_latex: C\sqrt{Td\log\left(1+\frac{TL}{\lambda d}\right)}\Bigg(\lambda^\frac{1}{2} \norm{\mathbf{w}^* - \mathbf{h}}_2 + R\sqrt{d \log(T + T^2 L/(\lambda d))}\Bigg)

symbols.dist_h: ||w* - h||_2, distance between bias vector and true parameter

conditions: x^T w* in [-1,1] for all arms

source.label: Lemma:RegretFixedBias
source.quote: (REG-OFUL Expected Regret) Under the same assumptions of Theorem 1, if in addition, for all $t$ and all $\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{D}_t$, $\mathbf{x}^\top \mathbf{w}^* \in [-1,1]$, and considering $\lambda \geq 1$, we have: $\overline{R}(T,\mathbf{w}^*) \leq C\sqrt{Td\log(1+\frac{TL}{\lambda d})}(\lambda^{1/2} \norm{\mathbf{w}^* - \mathbf{h}}_2 + R\sqrt{d \log(T + T^2 L/(\lambda d))})$ where ... $C>0$ is a constant factor.

results.notes: Unspecified constant C, recorded as O. R is the sub-Gaussian noise parameter (sigma). Requires oracle knowledge of ||h - w*|| for the confidence radius.

bound.expression_latex: C \sqrt{Td\log\bigg(1 + \frac{TL}{ \lambda d}\bigg)}\bigg(\lambda^\frac{1}{2}S+ R\sqrt{d \log(T + T^2 L/(\lambda d))}\bigg)

source.label: Cor:RightH
source.quote: (i) Independent Task Learning (ITL), given by setting $\mathbf{h} = \mathbf{0}$ satisfies ... $\overline{R}(T,\mathbf{w}^*) \leq C \sqrt{Td\log(1 + \frac{TL}{ \lambda d})}(\lambda^\frac{1}{2}S+ R\sqrt{d \log(T + T^2 L/(\lambda d))})$ which is of order $\bigO(d\sqrt{T})$ for any $\lambda\geq1$.

results.notes: ITL = BIAS-OFUL with h=0 (essentially OFUL). Paper says this is O(d sqrt(T)) up to logs.

bound.expression_latex: C \sqrt{Td\log\bigg(1 + \frac{TL}{ \lambda d}\bigg)} \bigg( R\sqrt{d \log(T + T^2 L/(\lambda d))}\bigg)

source.label: Cor:RightH
source.quote: (ii) The Oracle, given by setting $\mathbf{h}=\mathbf{w^*}$ satisfies $\overline{R}(T,\mathbf{w}^*) \leq C \sqrt{Td\log(1 + \frac{TL}{ \lambda d})} ( R\sqrt{d \log(T + T^2 L/(\lambda d))})$ which is $0$ as $\lambda\to\infty$.

results.notes: Oracle bias h = w*; bound tends to 0 as lambda -> infinity.

symbols.Mar_h: E_{w~rho} ||w - h||_2, mean absolute distance of bias h to tasks

conditions: task distribution rho has bounded support, ||w||_2 <= S

source.label: Lemma:TransferRegretBound
source.quote: (Transfer Regret Bound) Under the same conditions in Theorem 1 and Lemma 1, the expected transfer regret of BIAS-OFUL can be upper bounded as: $\mathcal{R}(T,\rho) \leq C \sqrt{Td \lambda \log(1 + \frac{TL}{\lambda d}) } \mar_\mathbf{h} + RCd\sqrt{T \log(T + \frac{T^2L}{\lambda d})\log(1+\frac{TL}{\lambda d})} \leq C \sqrt{Td \lambda \log(1 + \frac{TL}{\lambda d}) \var_\mathbf{h}} + ...$

results.notes: Transfer regret = regret averaged over task distribution rho (Bayesian-style). First inequality of Lemma 2.

conditions: task distribution rho has bounded support, ||w||_2 <= S

symbols.Var_0: E_{w~rho} ||w||_2^2, second moment of the task distribution

conditions: task distribution rho has bounded support, ||w||_2 <= S

source.label: Cor:RightHTransfer
source.quote: setting $\lambda = \frac{1}{T \Var_\mathbf{h}}$ ... (i) Independent Task Learning (ITL), given by setting the bias hypeparameter $\mathbf{h}$ equal to $\mathbf{0}$, satisfies $\mathcal{R}(T,\rho) \leq [1 + \sqrt{T d \log(T + \frac{T^3L\var_{\mathbf{0}}}{ d})}]C\sqrt{d \log(1+\frac{T^2L\var_{\mathbf{0}}}{ d})}$

results.notes: Note lambda=1/(T Var_h) may conflict with the lambda>=1 condition of Lemma 1; recorded as stated. R factor dropped in the paper's statement.

symbols.Var_wbar: E_{w~rho} ||w - wbar||_2^2, variance of the task distribution

conditions: task distribution rho has bounded support, ||w||_2 <= S

source.label: Cor:RightHTransfer
source.quote: (ii) The Oracle, given by setting the bias hyperparameter $\mathbf{h}$ equal to the mean task $\wbar$, satisfies $\mathcal{R}(T,\rho) \leq [1 + \sqrt{T d \log(T + \frac{T^3L\var_{\wbar}}{ d})}] C\sqrt{d \log(1+\frac{T^2L\var_{\wbar}}{ d})}$

results.notes: Oracle knows the mean task wbar.

symbols.eps_NT: mean estimation error ||wbar - hhat_{N,T}||_2^2, bounded by sqrt(eps_NT) <= H_rho(N+1, wbar) + max_j beta_j(1/T)/lambda_min^{1/2}(V_{j,T})

conditions: task distribution rho has bounded support, ||w||_2 <= S
tuning: bias = weighted average of per-task ridge estimates (Eq. ApproachA)

source.label: Th:TransferRegretBoundA
source.quote: Let the assumptions of Lemma 2 hold and let $\hhat_{N,t}^\lambda$ be defined as in Equation (ApproachA). Then, it hold that $\mathcal{R}(T,\rho) \leq d C\sqrt{T \log(1 + \frac{T^2L (\Var_\wbar + \epsilon_{N,T}(\rho) )}{d})}$ where the mean estimation error can be bound as $\sqrt{\epsilon_{N,T}(\rho)} \leq H_\rho(N+1, \wbar) + \max_{j=1,\dots,N} \frac{\beta^\lambda_j(1/T)}{\lambda^{1/2}_{\min}(\mathbf{V}^\lambda_{j,T})}$.

results.notes: Bound depends on a random, data-dependent estimation error; derivation from Lemma 2 is informal. N previous tasks.

symbols.eps_NT: mean estimation error, bounded by sqrt(eps_NT) <= S/(lam+nu_min) + 2(N+1) max_j Htilde(N+1,w_j) + R sqrt(2/(lam+nu_min) log(T(1+N T L^2/(lam d)))) + H_rho(N+1, wbar)
symbols.nu_min: lambda_min of the global design matrix over all tasks

conditions: task distribution rho has bounded support, ||w||_2 <= S
tuning: bias = global ridge regression over all past tasks (Eq. GlobalRR)

source.label: Th:TransferRegretBoundB
source.quote: Let the assumptions of Lemma 2 hold and let $\hhat^\lambda_{N,t}$ be defined as in Equation (GlobalRR). Then, the following upper bound holds $\mathcal{R}(T,\rho) \leq dC \sqrt{T \log(1 + \frac{T^2L (\Var_\wbar + \epsilon_{N,t}(\rho) )}{d})}$ where the mean estimation error can be bound as $\sqrt{\epsilon_{N,T}(\rho)} \leq \frac{S}{\lambda + \nu_{\min}} + 2(N+1) \max_{1\leq j\leq N+1} \widetilde{H}(N+1, \w_j) + R\sqrt{\frac{2}{\lambda + \nu_{\min}}\log(T(1 + \frac{N T L^2}{\lambda d}))} + H_\rho(N + 1,\wbar)$

results.notes: Data-dependent bound with bias term depending on task misalignment sigma_max(V_j Vtilde^{-1}).

cited_results.cited_title: Improved algorithms for linear stochastic bandits
cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic linear bandit, ||w*|| <= S, ||x|| <= L, R-sub-Gaussian noise; regret with probability at least 1-delta
